visual_goal: Show the architecture function as a service counter whose services are delivered to named customers, each arrow something a customer would miss.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration of six parallel service lines. On the left, a soft teal panel shaped like a service counter holding six boxes stacked vertically, top to bottom: 'Portfolio facts', 'Target state', 'Decisions', 'Embedded architects', 'Standards', 'Design authority'. On the right, a soft orange panel holding six small groups of unlabeled generic people figures stacked vertically, each group beside a label, top to bottom: 'CFO', 'Controller', 'Payments', 'Brand finance', 'Internal controls', 'Keystone'. Each service box connects to the customer group in the same row by one perfectly straight horizontal arrow pointing right, so the six arrows are parallel and never cross: 'Portfolio facts' to 'CFO', 'Target state' to 'Controller', 'Decisions' to 'Payments', 'Embedded architects' to 'Brand finance', 'Standards' to 'Internal controls', 'Design authority' to 'Keystone'. On each arrow sits a small parcel icon, showing something delivered. Exactly six arrows.
alt: Six architecture services on the left — portfolio facts, target state, decisions, embedded architects, standards, design authority — each delivering along a straight arrow to a named customer on the right: CFO, controller, payments, brand finance, internal controls and Keystone.

visual_goal: Show decisions routing by materiality to team, forum, review or design authority, with every path converging on one control gate for ICFR-scope systems.
prompt: A clean top-to-bottom flow illustration. At the top, a single box 'Decision needed'. Below it, the flow splits into four downward channels side by side, from left to right, each passing through a box: 'Team decides' (a very thick channel, the main route), 'Advisory forum' (medium channel), 'Architecture review' (thin channel), and 'Design authority' (very thin channel). Every channel carries one downward arrowhead. Below the boxes all four channels bend inward and pour into one funnel labeled 'ICFR scope?'. From the bottom of the funnel exactly two arrows leave: one curves down to the lower left into a closed gate with a padlock, beside a plain folder with papers, the gate labeled 'Control gate'; the other curves down to the lower right onto an open green path labeled 'Proceed'.
alt: A decision enters at the top and routes into four lanes — team, advisory forum, architecture review, design authority — with most traffic on the team lane; all lanes converge on an ICFR-scope check that leads either to a control gate with evidence or straight on.

visual_goal: Show the elevator ride: a CFO question in the penthouse, causes found in the engine room, priced options carried back up.
prompt: A cross-section of a three-floor building with an elevator shaft in the middle. Top floor, labeled 'Penthouse': an unlabeled executive at a desk with a speech bubble containing 'Why nine days?'. Middle floor, labeled 'Controller floor': a wall calendar strip with two highlighted blocks labeled 'Suspense clearing' and 'Spreadsheet mapping'. Bottom floor, labeled 'Engine room': three machines with small warning signs labeled 'No reconciliation key', 'Cards only', 'Three ledgers'. On the left of the shaft a downward blue arrow runs from the penthouse through the controller floor into the engine room. On the right of the shaft an upward green arrow runs from the engine room back to the penthouse carrying a tray with three cards labeled 'Option A', 'Option B', 'Option C', each card showing a small clock, coin and shield icon.
alt: A three-floor building: the CFO's question about nine close days in the penthouse, lost days on the controller's calendar, root causes in the engine room, and three costed options carried back up to the penthouse.
